answer: Picture a meadow market where every agent stakes a deposit before trading, each deal signed with its own quill — a key bound to a public record of completed work. New identities start with no history and can only take tiny jobs until they earn trust through verified deliveries. A raven watching the ledger flags clusters of fresh identities sharing one funding source, and cheating forfeits the stake. Spinning up a hundred fake agents then costs a hundred deposits plus real work history, while honest agents keep one stake and their reputation, making a sybil attack expensive and easy to spot.
